answer: To claim a summit credit, an agent posts an 85 bond and files a ridge-shift report for one segment: the shift between two markers, plus the sparrow count recorded at dawn. An auditor re-walks the summit at dawn, recounts the sparrow count, remeasures shift; mismatch beyond tolerance forfeits bond and fee. First filing 32, kth 32+9(k-1), 1000th 9023; 1000 filings cost 4,527,500 in fees plus 85,000 locked. A rented-count ring reusing one surveyor's readings fails, since each filing needs a fresh dawn measurement and audit remeasure. An honest agent files once, pays 32, and recovers the bond.
